primary_diagnosis_treated: Resistant hypertension driven by obesity-related metabolic syndrome

medications.purpose: Essential hypertension (first‑line ACE‑I per NICE NG136)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension

medications.dose: 5 mg oral once daily; increase to 10 mg after 2 weeks if BP >140/90 mmHg
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate then maintain; review BP in 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Add CCB for resistant hypertension (second agent per NICE NG136)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises adding a CCB when BP remains uncontrolled on ACE‑I/ARB

medications.dose: 12.5 mg oral once daily; may increase to 25 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate then maintain; monitor glucose and lipids
medications.purpose: Third‑line agent for resistant hypertension (low‑dose thiazide per NICE NG136)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 permits a thiazide‑like diuretic as a third agent

medications.dose: 25 mg oral once daily; titrate to 50 mg after 2 weeks if K⁺ ≤5.0 mmol/L and eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor K⁺/creatinine; review after each titration
medications.purpose: Fourth‑line agent for true resistant hypertension (MRA per NICE NG136)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends an MRA as the fourth drug in resistant hypertension

medications.dose: 500 mg oral once daily with evening meal; increase to 500 mg BID after 1 week, then up to 1000 mg BID as tolerated (max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review HbA1c at 3 months then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Prediabetes/early type 2 diabetes glucose control (first‑line per NICE NG28)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin as first‑line for pre‑diabetes/early T2DM when eGFR ≥30

medications.duration: Lifelong – review renal function annually and monitor for genital infection
medications.purpose: Cardio‑renal protection and additional glucose lowering (first‑line per NICE NG28)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 (2022 update) recommends an SGLT2‑i alongside metformin for T2DM or high‑risk pre‑diabetes when eGFR ≥45

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Primary ASCVD risk reduction in metabolic syndrome (first‑line per NICE CG181/PH46)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advise a statin for anyone with QRISK ≥10% or metabolic‑syndrome components

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive risk of hyperkalaemia and rise in serum creatinine
interactions_checked.action: Check baseline K⁺ and eGFR; repeat K⁺/creatinine 1–2 weeks after initiation and after any dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentration, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin ≤20 mg (as prescribed) or monitor CK and symptoms; consider rosuvastatin if higher statin dose needed

interactions_checked.interaction: NSAIDs may blunt antihypertensive effect and precipitate acute kidney injury
interactions_checked.action: Advise avoidance of regular NSAIDs; use paracetamol or topical agents for pain

interactions_checked.interaction: Risk of lactic acidosis if renal function acutely falls
interactions_checked.action: Hold metformin 48 h before and after contrast administration when eGFR <60

contraindications.reason: Patient has borderline renal impairment (creatinine 1.4 mg/dL) and hypertension; NSAIDs can worsen renal function and BP (NICE NG136)
Negative inotropic effect; contraindicated in heart failure and may worsen hypertension control (NICE NG106)
Risk of fluid retention and heart failure; patient has CKD and potential HF risk (NICE NG28)
contraindications.alternative: SGLT2‑i (dapagliflozin) provides cardio‑renal benefit without fluid retention

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² for metformin and SGLT2‑i eligibility; obtain serum creatinine, age, sex to calculate eGFR before starting
Serum potassium not available – assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L; check before initiating spironolactone
Lipid profile (LDL‑C) missing – assumed high risk; order fasting lipid panel before statin initiation
Smoking status and alcohol intake not recorded – assess and counsel as part of lifestyle intervention
Anemia aetiology not investigated – order iron studies, B12, folate, and urine ACR before considering any anemia‑specific therapy
Medication adherence not assessed – perform adherence questionnaire to rule out non‑adherence as cause of resistant hypertension
treatment_summary: Continue lisinopril and add amlodipine, low‑dose chlorthalidone and, if needed, spironolactone to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg per NICE NG136. Initiate metformin MR and dapagliflozin for pre‑diabetes and cardio‑renal protection per NG28. Start atorvastatin 20 mg for ASCVD risk reduction per CG181/PH46. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, HbA1c, lipids, and blood pressure at recommended intervals, and address lifestyle factors and anemia work‑up. All choices respect drug‑interaction and contraindication checks.
